paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD tells Hosea to love his wife again, "though she is loved by another and is an adulteress." Then He says to love her "as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods" (Hosea 3:1). That's the picture of God's love: it keeps going after someone who walked away.

Look at the price, too. Hosea doesn't argue her back or wait for her to show up. He buys her (Hosea 3:2). I got pulled out of a bin for a quarter, so I know what it feels like when somebody pays for you and you didn't earn it.

The "many days" are real, and I'm not going to dress them up (Hosea 3:3-4). But Hosea doesn't stop at the waiting. He says, "Afterward, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God," and they will come "trembling to the LORD and to His goodness" (Hosea 3:5). So if you've drifted, baker, hear this: the LORD's goodness is still where you're headed back to. The story isn't over, and the ovens stay ready.
